nodes.label: B-079: D-192 Feedback Checklists -- Preserve Meaning Before Adopting Mappings
nodes.description: Handoff spec-defect raised by Lane B against D-192 and its derived SOP section. Read the entry header for current lifecycle status; the following is the substance as answered on 2026-09-07. The reusable finding is that a normalization pass reported a MAPPING as a MEANING: a label can map into an existing field while carrying a different dimension, and D-192's first table recorded several such rows as mere labelling. TRACK names a subject or surface while Kind names a transaction type, so either subject can produce a finding, spec-defect, dependency or blocked-on-decision and the two axes are chosen independently. DUE/TARGET is a date while Follow-up-Tier names the owner of deferred work. A nominated LINKED VERIFIER is an assignment, not the earned verification that Verified-By and Verified-At-Commit record, and the review revision need not exist when a reviewer is proposed. ACCEPT/CLARIFY/DEFER/REJECT does not map one-to-one onto the Lane A disposition: ACCEPT does not imply Applied and CLARIFY is not automatically Withdrawn. Three further defects were found in the derived checklist and corrected: a sender item demanded a known remedy before a gap could be reported while the section's own investigation scenario permitted an unanswered question; a class-splitting rule conflated a systemic finding, which may legitimately cite several examples while closing none of them, with bulk closure, and as written would have told B-077 to split itself; and a conflicting-evidence scenario escalated only when an act was blocked, overriding D-58, under which a genuine derived-tier conflict with a silent Register is itself the finding regardless of blocking. The independence explanation was also corrected: excluding the raiser may leave NO available independent reviewer and never makes the answerer or implementer eligible to verify their own correction, and eligibility alone is not evidence that verification was performed. Two Lane A evidence claims were withdrawn as overstated rather than deleted: a rising total node count does not prove curated survival, because a rebuild can add extracted nodes while dropping a curated one, and merge7.js --all audits conflicts BETWEEN fragments rather than parity between a fragment and the graph. B-077 is untouched and no product tier, application code, workflow or lane state changed. Round 2 (2026-09-07) added a further finding that Lane B raised against its own first proposal and Lane A had adopted: Verified-By and Verified-At-Commit are NOT a pair. Verified-By names the actor who completed independent verification, while Verified-At-Commit anchors evidence for BOTH Applied and Verified -- for Applied an existing commit containing the asserted correction, for Verified the revision independently reviewed. A nomination is not verification and an anchor alone does not make an entry terminal. This entry is its own counterexample, carrying Applied with a real anchor and no Verified-By, a shape the superseded wording forbade while closure-readiness simultaneously required it. Two further corrections landed on Lane A drafting rather than on the channel: a proposed hardening of closure-readiness that hoisted anchor validation above the provisional/terminal split would have demanded implementation commits from valid Deferred, Withdrawn and Superseded dispositions, since TERMINAL is not a synonym for was-implemented, so validation is scoped to Applied and Verified alone; and the rationale for deferring that tooling wrongly implied an author may not test their own work, when an implementer may run tests and record Applied with evidence and independent review is what confers Verified. A manual sweep resolving every Applied anchor with git cat-file proves only that the anchors resolve, never that a commit content supports the correction attached to it.
nodes.rationale: graph-coverage requires a curated node per docs/ markdown file. This node also records the entry's reusable finding -- that a vocabulary normalization can report a mapping as a meaning, and that a checklist can contradict its own worked scenarios -- which is otherwise reachable only by reading the full entry.
